NASAFI:107:5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:107:5/r1.claim: The warning continues by specifying the worshippers meant: those heedless of prayer, who show off and withhold alms or useful aid.
NASAFI:107:5/r1.anchor: { فَوَيْلٌ لّلْمُصَلّينَ الذين هُمْ عَن صلاتهم سَاهُونَ الذين هُمْ يُرَاءونَ

NASAFI:107:5/r2.speaker: author

NASAFI:107:5/r2.anchor: يعني بهذا المنافقين لا يصلونها سراً ؛ لأنهم لا يعتقدون وجوبها

NASAFI:107:5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:107:5/r3.claim: Another description is hypocrites who outwardly count themselves among worshippers but neglect prayer, seek neither nearness nor fulfillment of duty, go through motions mindlessly, display worship, and withhold alms and useful things.
NASAFI:107:5/r3.anchor: وقيل : فويل للمنافقين الذين يدخلون أنفسهم في جملة المصلين صورة

NASAFI:107:5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:5/r4.speaker: أنس والحسن
NASAFI:107:5/r4.claim: Anas and al-Ḥasan say “about their prayer” means neglecting and turning away from it, the behavior of hypocrites; “within their prayer” would mean distraction by Satan or one's thoughts, which also befalls Muslims, including the Prophet.
NASAFI:107:5/r4.anchor: وعن أنس والحسن قالا : الحمد لله الذي قال { عَن صلاتهم } ولم يقل

NASAFI:107:5/r5.speaker: أنس والحسن
NASAFI:107:5/r5.claim: They distinguish forgetfulness “in prayer,” caused by Satanic whisper or one's thoughts, from neglecting prayer; this ordinary distraction may affect any Muslim, and the Prophet himself sometimes forgot in prayer.
NASAFI:107:5/r5.anchor: ومعنى «في » أن السهو يعتريهم فيها بوسوسة شيطان أو حديث نفس

NASAFI:107:5/r6.anchor: والمراءاة مفاعلة من الإراءة ؛ لأن المرائي يرائي الناس عمله

NASAFI:107:5/r7.anchor: ولا يكون الرجل مرائياً بإظهار الفرائض

NASAFI:107:6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:6/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI:107:6/r3.claim: An alternative says these hypocrites only outwardly join the praying, neglect prayer without seeking nearness to God or fulfilling its duty, mechanically bow and rise, display compliance, and withhold zakat and useful goods.
NASAFI:107:6/r3.anchor: وقيل : فويل للمنافقين الذين يدخلون أنفسهم في جملة المصلين صورة وهم غافلون عن صلاتهم

NASAFI:107:6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:6/r4.speaker: أنس والحسن
NASAFI:107:6/r4.claim: Anas and al-Hasan praise عن صلاتهم rather than في صلاتهم: عن means neglect amounting to abandonment and inattention, a hypocrite trait; في would mean lapses during prayer from satanic whispering or self-talk, which no Muslim escapes.
NASAFI:107:6/r4.anchor: وعن أنس والحسن قالا : الحمد لله الذي قال { عَن صلاتهم } ولم يقل «في صلاتهم »

NASAFI:107:6/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:6/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI:107:6/r5.claim: Nasafi adds that the Prophet himself experienced forgetfulness in prayer, let alone others.
NASAFI:107:6/r5.anchor: وذلك لا يخلو عنه مسلم . وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقع له السهو في صلاته فضلاً عن غيره

NASAFI:107:7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:7/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI:107:7/r3.claim: An alternative says these hypocrites only outwardly join the praying, neglect prayer without seeking nearness to God or fulfilling its duty, mechanically bow and rise, display compliance, and withhold zakat and useful goods.
NASAFI:107:7/r3.anchor: وقيل : فويل للمنافقين الذين يدخلون أنفسهم في جملة المصلين صورة وهم غافلون عن صلاتهم

NASAFI:107:7/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:7/r4.speaker: أنس والحسن
NASAFI:107:7/r4.claim: Anas and al-Hasan praise عن صلاتهم rather than في صلاتهم: عن means neglect amounting to abandonment and inattention, a hypocrite trait; في would mean lapses during prayer from satanic whispering or self-talk, which no Muslim escapes.
NASAFI:107:7/r4.anchor: وعن أنس والحسن قالا : الحمد لله الذي قال { عَن صلاتهم } ولم يقل «في صلاتهم »

NASAFI:107:7/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:7/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI:107:7/r5.claim: Nasafi adds that the Prophet himself experienced forgetfulness in prayer, let alone others.
NASAFI:107:7/r5.anchor: وذلك لا يخلو عنه مسلم . وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقع له السهو في صلاته فضلاً عن غيره

QURTUBI:107:5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:5/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:107:5/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the prayer-neglecter as one who expects no reward for praying and fears no punishment for abandoning prayer.
QURTUBI:107:5/r1.anchor: فروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال : هو المصلي الذي إن صلى لم يرج لها ثوابا

QURTUBI:107:5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:107:5/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas also says they delay their prayers beyond their appointed times.
QURTUBI:107:5/r2.anchor: وعنه أيضا : الذين يؤخرونها عن أوقاتها

QURTUBI:107:5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:5/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
QURTUBI:107:5/r3.claim: Ibrahim, in a report from al-Mughira, explains the lapse as wasting prayer time.
QURTUBI:107:5/r3.anchor: وكذا روى المغيرة عن إبراهيم ، قال : ساهون بإضاعة الوقت

QURTUBI:107:5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:5/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
QURTUBI:107:5/r4.claim: Abu al-Aliya says they fail to pray on time and do not complete bowing or prostration.
QURTUBI:107:5/r4.anchor: وعن أبي العالية : لا يصلونها لمواقيتها ، ولا يتمون ركوعها ولا سجودها

QURTUBI:107:5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:5/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:107:5/r5.claim: Qurtubi says the warning that later people abandoned prayer in Maryam supports the interpretation of neglecting its times.
QURTUBI:107:5/r5.anchor: قلت : ويدل على هذا قوله تعالى : { فخلف من بعدهم خلف أضاعوا الصلاة }

QURTUBI:107:5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:5/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
QURTUBI:107:5/r6.claim: Another report from Ibrahim describes someone who raises his head from prostration while turning his gaze aside.
QURTUBI:107:5/r6.anchor: وروي عن إبراهيم أيضا : أنه الذي إذا سجد قام برأسه هكذا ملتفتا

QURTUBI:107:5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:5/r7.speaker: قطرب
QURTUBI:107:5/r7.claim: Qutrub interprets the lapse as failing to recite or remember God.
QURTUBI:107:5/r7.anchor: وقال قطرب : هو ألا يقرأ ولا يذكر الله

QURTUBI:107:5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:5/r8.speaker: عبد الله
QURTUBI:107:5/r8.claim: Abdullah's reading has lāhūn, ‘heedless,’ in place of sāhūn.
QURTUBI:107:5/r8.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله " الذين هم عن صلاتهم لاهون "

QURTUBI:107:5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:5/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:107:5/r9.claim: The Prophet explains the verse as people who negligently postpone prayer until after its proper time; Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas transmits this report.
QURTUBI:107:5/r9.anchor: وقال سعد بن أبي وقاص : قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله :

QURTUBI:107:5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:5/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:107:5/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says these are hypocrites who leave prayer in private but perform it in public, as in 4:142.
QURTUBI:107:5/r10.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا : هم المنافقون يتركون الصلاة سرا ، يصلونها علانية

QURTUBI:107:5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:5/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI:107:5/r11.claim: Qurtubi takes the following description of people who show off as evidence that the prayer-neglecters are hypocrites.
QURTUBI:107:5/r11.anchor: ويدل على أنها في المنافقين قوله : { الذين هم يراؤون }

QURTUBI:107:5/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:5/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:107:5/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says that had the verse said ‘heedless in their prayer,’ it would have described believers.
QURTUBI:107:5/r12.anchor: وقال ابن وهب عن مالك : قال ابن عباس : ولو قال في صلاتهم ساهون لكانت في المؤمنين

QURTUBI:107:5/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:5/r13.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI:107:5/r13.claim: Ata praises the verse for saying ‘about their prayer’ rather than ‘in their prayer.’
QURTUBI:107:5/r13.anchor: وقال عطاء : الحمد لله الذي قال { عن صلاتهم } ، ولم يقل في صلاتهم

QURTUBI:107:5/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:5/r14.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI:107:5/r14.claim: Al-Zamakhshari distinguishes neglecting prayer through abandonment and indifference, characteristic of hypocrites or brazen sinners, from incidental distraction during prayer.
QURTUBI:107:5/r14.anchor: قال الزمخشري : فإن قلت : أي فرق بين قوله : { عن صلاتهم } ، وبين قولك : في صلاتهم ؟ قلت : معنى " عن " أنهم ساهون عنها سهو ترك لها

QURTUBI:107:5/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:5/r15.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI:107:5/r15.claim: Al-Zamakhshari notes that distraction during prayer is nearly unavoidable even for Muslims, including the Prophet, so jurists discuss the prostration of forgetfulness.
QURTUBI:107:5/r15.anchor: قال الزمخشري : فإن قلت : أي فرق بين قوله : { عن صلاتهم } ، وبين قولك : في صلاتهم ؟ قلت : معنى " عن "

QURTUBI:107:5/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:5/r16.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI:107:5/r16.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says avoiding forgetfulness is impossible; the Prophet and Companions forgot, while those who never forget fail to reflect on prayer and attend only to its count; prophetic lapses came from greater thoughts or satanic distraction.
QURTUBI:107:5/r16.anchor: قال ابن العربي : لأن السلامة من السهو محال ، وقد سها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في صلاته والصحابة

RAZI:107:4/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:4/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:107:4/r6.claim: The threatened traits are heedlessness about prayer, ostentation, and withholding small assistance; all are sins, but do not ordinarily make someone a hypocrite, prompting exegetes to explain the severe threat.
RAZI:107:4/r6.anchor: الآية دالة على حصول التهديد العظيم بفعل ثلاثة أمور

RAZI:107:4/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:4/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:107:4/r7.claim: The relied-upon answer restricts the warning to hypocrites who perform these acts; it implies disbelievers incur extra punishment for forbidden acts and neglected duties, supporting al-Shāfiʿī’s view that they are addressed by the branches of religious law.
RAZI:107:4/r7.anchor: أن قوله : { فويل للمصلين } أي فويل للمصلين من المنافقين الذين يأتون بهذه الأفعال

RAZI:107:4/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:4/r8.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
RAZI:107:4/r8.claim: ʿAṭāʾ reports Ibn ʿAbbās’s distinction: “in their prayer” could threaten believers, but “about their prayer” describes those who forget prayer and are empty of it.
RAZI:107:4/r8.anchor: ما رواه عطاء عن ابن عباس أنه لو قال الله : في صلاتهم ساهون

RAZI:107:4/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:4/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:107:4/r9.claim: Al-Rāzī calls that explanation weak: treating heedlessness about prayer as abandoning it conflicts with their being called worshippers, and abandonment alone is neither hypocrisy nor unbelief.
RAZI:107:4/r9.anchor: وهذا القول ضعيف لأن السهو عن الصلاة لا يجوز أن يكون مفسرا بترك الصلاة

RAZI:107:4/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:4/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:107:4/r10.claim: A possible reply says they are misleaders outwardly but have forgotten prayer inwardly, like the hypocrites described in 4:142 as lazy, ostentatious, and remembering God only a little.
RAZI:107:4/r10.anchor: كما قال : { وإذا قاموا إلى الصلاة قاموا كسالى يراءون الناس

RAZI:107:4/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:4/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:107:4/r11.claim: Another reply distinguishes a hypocrite who forgets God throughout prayer from a believer who may become heedless in only some parts; this makes heedlessness in prayer a believer’s lapse and heedlessness about prayer a disbeliever’s trait.
RAZI:107:4/r11.anchor: فثبت أن السهو في الصلاة من أفعال المؤمن والسهو عن الصلاة من أفعال الكافر

RAZI:107:4/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:4/r12.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص ومسروق والحسن ومقاتل
RAZI:107:4/r12.claim: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, Masrūq, al-Ḥasan, and Muqātil say the heedless are those who fail to observe prayer times and conditions and do not care whether they pray.
RAZI:107:4/r12.anchor: وهو قول سعد بن أبي وقاص ومسروق والحسن ومقاتل

RAZI:107:4/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:4/r13.speaker: كثير من العلماء
RAZI:107:4/r13.claim: Many scholars hold that the Prophet never lapsed in prayer; rather, God allowed him to perform the act of a forgetful person so that he could demonstrate the law, since practical demonstration is stronger.
RAZI:107:4/r13.anchor: فقال كثير من العلماء : إنه عليه الصلاة والسلام ما سها ، لكن الله تعالى أذن له

RAZI:107:4/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:4/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:107:4/r14.claim: The Prophet’s and Companions’ prayer lapses are repaired either by prostration of forgetfulness or by sunnah and voluntary prayers.
RAZI:107:4/r14.anchor: سهو الرسول والصحابة وذلك منجبر تارة بسجود السهو وتارة بالسنن والنوافل

RAZI:107:4/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:4/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:107:4/r15.claim: A second kind is inattentiveness during prayer, including failure to keep religious knowledge and intentions present.
RAZI:107:4/r15.anchor: ما يكون في الصلاة من الغفلة وعدم استحضار المعارف والنيات

RAZI:107:4/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:4/r16.speaker: author
RAZI:107:4/r16.claim: A third kind is leaving prayer without making it up and taking it outside its time; the hypocrite’s performative prayer is worse than simply abandoning prayer because it mocks religion.
RAZI:107:4/r16.anchor: الترك لا إلى قضاء والإخراج عن الوقت ، ومن ذلك صلاة المنافق وهي شر من ترك الصلاة

RAZI:107:5/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:5/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:107:5/r1.claim: The discussion follows orphan abuse and failure to urge feeding: mistreatment wrongs creatures, while prayer without reverence is worse because it neglects service to the Creator.
RAZI:107:5/r1.anchor: لأن الإيذاء والمنع من النفع معاملة مع المخلوق

RAZI:107:5/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:5/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:107:5/r2.claim: The verse answers the objection that prayer deters indecency: these worshipers’ prayer itself is made up of ostentation and heedlessness.
RAZI:107:5/r2.anchor: الصلاة كيف تنهاه عن هذا الفعل المنكر

RAZI:107:5/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:5/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:107:5/r3.claim: Neglecting compassion toward creation and reverence for God completes their wretchedness; “woe” marks a grave crime, as in three other warnings.
RAZI:107:5/r3.anchor: واعلم أن هذا اللفظ إنما يستعمل عند الجريمة الشديدة

RAZI:107:5/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:5/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:107:5/r4.claim: A report says each person in Hell wails according to his sin, including love of status, pre-Islamic zeal, or prayer; one should say, “Woe to me if God does not forgive me.”
RAZI:107:5/r4.anchor: ويروى أن كل أحد ينوح في النار بحسب جريمته

RAZI:107:5/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:5/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:107:5/r5.claim: The severe threat concerns three acts—heedlessness about prayer, showing off, and withholding al-maʿūn—raising the question why sins that do not by themselves make one an unbeliever draw such punishment.
RAZI:107:5/r5.anchor: الآية دالة على حصول التهديد العظيم بفعل ثلاثة أمور

RAZI:107:5/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:5/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:107:5/r6.claim: The relied-upon answer reads “those who pray” as hypocrites who commit these acts, so the threat is directed at them.
RAZI:107:5/r6.anchor: أي فويل للمصلين من المنافقين الذين يأتون بهذه الأفعال

RAZI:107:5/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:5/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:107:5/r7.claim: On this reading, unbelievers receive additional punishment for violating prohibitions and neglecting obligations, supporting al-Shāfiʿī’s view that they are addressed by the law’s subsidiary commands.
RAZI:107:5/r7.anchor: وهو يدل على صحة قول الشافعي

RAZI:107:5/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:5/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:107:5/r8.claim: ʿAṭāʾ transmits Ibn ʿAbbās’s distinction: “heedless in their prayer” would threaten believers, whereas “heedless from their prayer” describes people who do not remember it and are detached from it.
RAZI:107:5/r8.anchor: ما رواه عطاء عن ابن عباس

RAZI:107:5/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:5/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:107:5/r9.claim: Rāzī calls Ibn ʿAbbās’s explanation weak: heedlessness from prayer cannot mean simply abandoning it, since the verse calls them worshipers, and such abandonment alone is neither hypocrisy nor unbelief.
RAZI:107:5/r9.anchor: وهذا القول ضعيف لأن السهو عن الصلاة لا يجوز

RAZI:107:5/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:5/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:107:5/r10.claim: Rāzī answers that they count as worshipers outwardly but have forgotten prayer altogether inwardly, as hypocrites rise lazily, show off, and remember God only a little.
RAZI:107:5/r10.anchor: حكم عليهم بكونهم مضلين نظرا إلى الصورة

RAZI:107:5/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:5/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:107:5/r11.claim: Complete failure to remember God in every part of prayer reflects a hypocrite’s belief that prayer is useless; a believer may instead become inattentive during some parts, so heedlessness “in” prayer differs from heedlessness “from” it.
RAZI:107:5/r11.anchor: بل قد يحصل له السهو في الصلاة بمعنى أنه يصير ساهيا

RAZI:107:5/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:5/r12.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص ومسروق والحسن ومقاتل
RAZI:107:5/r12.claim: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, Masrūq, al-Ḥasan, and Muqātil explain the phrase as failing to guard prayer times and conditions and not caring whether one prays.
RAZI:107:5/r12.anchor: وهو قول سعد بن أبي وقاص ومسروق والحسن ومقاتل

RAZI:107:5/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:5/r13.speaker: كثير من العلماء
RAZI:107:5/r13.claim: Many scholars say the Prophet did not truly lapse in prayer; God enabled him to perform an act resembling a lapse so that he could demonstrate the law, whose practical demonstration is stronger.
RAZI:107:5/r13.anchor: الله تعالى أذن له في ذلك الفعل

RAZI:107:5/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:5/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:107:5/r14.claim: One category is lapses by the Prophet and Companions, repaired either by the prostration of forgetfulness or by sunnah and voluntary prayers.
RAZI:107:5/r14.anchor: سهو الرسول والصحابة وذلك منجبر تارة بسجود السهو

RAZI:107:5/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:5/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:107:5/r15.claim: A second category is distraction within prayer, including failure to summon one’s knowledge and intentions.
RAZI:107:5/r15.anchor: ما يكون في الصلاة من الغفلة وعدم استحضار المعارف والنيات

RAZI:107:5/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:5/r16.speaker: author
RAZI:107:5/r16.claim: A third category is leaving prayer without making it up and letting its time pass; a hypocrite’s token prayer is worse than leaving prayer because it mocks religion.
RAZI:107:5/r16.anchor: ومن ذلك صلاة المنافق وهي شر من ترك الصلاة

RAZI:107:6/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:6/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:107:6/r8.claim: The warning about heedlessness covers missing prayer time and inattentiveness within prayer; this verse adds ostentation, so prayer should be free of all three faults.
RAZI:107:6/r8.anchor: فظهر أن الصلاة يجب أن تكون خالية عن هذه الأحوال الثلاثة
